{{nihongo|'''Miyake Shrine'''|三宅神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ise Province]].

'''Miyake Shrine''' (みやけじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Kō-chō, {{ill|Suzuka, Mie|Q207311|qid=Q207311}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Mie|af|Mie-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Mie|ar|ميه (محافظة)|ast|Prefeutura de Mie|az|Mie prefekturası|azb|میه اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Mié|be|Міэ|bg|Мие|bn|মিয়ে প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Mie|cdo|Mie-gâing|ce|Ми (префектура)|ceb|Mie-ken|ckb|پارێزگای میێ|cs|Prefektura Mie|cy|Mie (talaith)|da|Mie-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Mie|eo|Gubernio Mie|es|Prefectura de Mie|et|Mie prefektuur|eu|Mie (prefektura)|fa|استان میه|fi|Mien prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Mie|frr|Mie (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Mie|gl|Prefectura de Mie|hak|Mie-yen|he|מיאה (מחוז)|hi|मिऐ प्रीफेक्चर|hr|Mie (prefektura)|hu|Mie prefektúra|hy|Միե (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Mie|ilo|Prepektura ti Mie|it|Prefettura di Mie|ja|三重県|ka|მიეს პრეფექტურა|km|មីអិ(ខេត្ត)|ko|미에현|la|Mieensis|lt|Mijės prefektūra|lv|Mie prefektūra|mk|Мие (префектура)|mn|Миэ муж|mni|ꯃꯤꯏ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|मिई प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Mie|ne|मिए|nl|Mie (prefectuur)|no|Mie (prefektur)|nov|Mie Prefekture|os|Миэ|pam|Prepektura ning Mie|pl|Prefektura Mie|pnb|ضلع مائی|pt|Mie|ro|Prefectura Mie|ru|Миэ|se|Mie prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Mie|si|මියේ ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Mie Prefecture|sk|Mie (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Мије|su|Préféktur Mie|sv|Mie prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Mie|tg|Префектураи Мие|th|จังหวัดมิเอะ|tl|Prepektura ng Mie|tr|Mie|tt|Ми (префектура)|uk|Префектура Міє|ur|میہ پریفیکچر|vi|Mie|war|Mie (prefektura)|wuu|三重县|zh|三重县|zh_classical|三重縣|zh_min_nan|Mie-koān|zh_yue|三重縣|qid=Q128196}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, is presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}} of {{ill|Ise Province|be|Ісэ (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیسێ|cs|Provincie Ise|de|Provinz Ise|es|Provincia de Ise|eu|Ise probintzia|fa|ولایت ایسه|fi|Isen provinssi|fr|Province d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

At the end of the Meiji period it merged '''E Shrine''' (えじんじゃ, former village shrine), another candidate shrine for a shikinaisha.

=== Enshrined deities ===
Current enshrined deities are the following three<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Office).</ref>.
* {{ill|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|ca|Kunitokotatchi|es|Kunitokotachi|fr|Kunitokotachi|it|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|ja|国之常立神|mni|ꯀꯨꯅꯤ-ꯅꯣ-ꯇꯣꯀꯣꯇꯆꯤ|ru|Куни-но токотати-но микото|simple|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|th|คูนิ โนะ โทโกตาจิ|uk|Куні но токотаті но камі|zh|國常立尊|qid=Q478504|lt=Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōanamuchi-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto}} - deity of the merged E Shrine.

In Meiji shrine registers, the deities are listed as Kuninotokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōanamuchi-no-Mikoto, and {{ill|Toyouke-hime|abstract|Q2983724|bcl|Toyoukebime|es|Toyouke Ōmikami|fr|Toyouke Ōmikami|ja|トヨウケビメ|kk|Тоёукэ бимэ|ru|Тоёукэ бимэ|simple|Toyōke Ōmikami|sv|Toyouke Ōmikami|tok|jan sewi suli Tojoke|zh|豐宇氣毘賣神|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-hime-no-Mikoto}}{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}. It is also said that after Meiji-end mergers of village shrines in Kō-chō, 24 deities are now enshrined{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.

d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166}}, and this shrine is regarded as a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for that shikinaisha{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}. Another candidate is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Miyake Shrine}} in Miyake-chō, Suzuka{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}. “Miyake” is thought to derive from ancient court-controlled lands called {{ill|Miyake|Q11465761|qid=Q11465761}}; from that viewpoint, Miyake-chō is often considered more plausible as the location of Suzuka’s miyake and the shikinaisha “Miyake Shrine”{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}. This shrine, by contrast, was commonly called “Sōsha Daimyōjin” until the Edo period, and appears to have been renamed “Miyake Shrine” only after Meiji; no old example of this site being called “Miyake Shrine” is known{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.

Regarding this shikinaisha “Miyake Shrine,” a possible relation has also been pointed out to “Kokushi no kami Miyake no Muraji Iwatoko” in the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'', entry for June 24, first year of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}} ({{ill|672|ab|672|af|672|als|672|am|672 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|672|ar|672|ary|672|ast|672|az|672|azb|۶۷۲ (میلادی)|be|672|be_x_old|672|bg|672|bn|৬৭২|bpy|মারি ৬৭২|br|672|bs|672.|ca|672|cdo|672 nièng|ceb|672|ckb|٦٧٢|crh|672|cs|672|cv|672|cy|672|da|672|de|672|el|672|eml|672|eo|672|es|672|et|672|eu|672|fa|۶۷۲ (میلادی)|fi|672|fo|672|fr|672|frr|672|fy|672|ga|672|gan|672年|gd|672|gl|672|he|672|hi|672|hr|672.|ht|672 (almanak jilyen)|hu|672|hy|672|id|672|io|672|is|672|it|672|ja|672年|jv|672|ka|672|kk|672 жыл|ko|672년|la|672|lb|672|lij|672|lmo|672|lt|672 m.|lv|672. gads|map_bms|672|mdf|672|mg|672|mhr|672|mk|672|mr|इ.स. ६७२|mrj|672 и|ms|672|mzn|۶۷۲|nah|672|nap|672|nds|672|nds_nl|672|new|सन् ६७२|nl|672|nn|672|no|672|nrm|672|nso|672|oc|672|or|୬୭୨|os|672-æм аз|pl|672|pnb|672|pt|672|qu|672|ro|672|ru|672 год|rue|672|sa|६७२|scn|672|sd|672ع|se|672|sh|672.|shn|672|si|672|sk|672|sl|672|sq|672|sr|672|su|672|sv|672|sw|672|tg|Соли 672|th|พ.ศ. 1215|tk|672|tl|672|tly|672|tr|672|tt|672 ел|uk|672|ur|672ء|uz|672|vec|672|vi|672|war|672|wuu|672年|xmf|672|zh|672年|zh_min_nan|672 nî|zh_yue|672年|qid=Q30601}}), when Prince Ōama (later Emperor Tenmu) reached Ise Suzuka{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. Another theory identifies this shrine instead with “Ōshika Miyake Shrine” in {{ill|Kawawa district|Q11553861|qid=Q11553861}}{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.

There is also a known theory placing this shrine as the sōsha of Ise Province{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. A sōsha is a shrine near a provincial capital where provincial deities were jointly enshrined, appearing nationwide from around the {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292}}. For Ise Province, the mid-{{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}} provincial office site has been identified as the Chōjayashiki ruins (national historic site “Ise Kokufu ruins”) away from Miyake Shrine, but the later Nara to Heian provincial office site remains uncertain, with one theory placing it around present Kō-chō where this shrine stands<ref name="伊勢国府跡"/><ref>“Ise Kokufu,” ''Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 24: Place Names of Mie Prefecture'', Heibonsha, 1983.</ref>. Around Kō-chō, remains related to the provincial capital have been found at Miyake Shrine ruins and Tennōyama-nishi ruins, but the core kokuga site has not been discovered<ref name="伊勢国府跡">{{PDFlink|[http://www.edu.city.suzuka.mie.jp/museum/kokufu-p.pdf "National Historic Site Ise Kokufu Ruins - Excavation of Chōjayashiki Site, Suzuka, Mie"]}} (Suzuka Archaeological Museum).</ref><ref>[http://www.edu.city.suzuka.mie.jp/museum/site100/0495.htm Miyake Shrine Ruins] (Suzuka Archaeological Museum website).</ref>. If the shrine name “Miyake” is assumed to be old in origin (not created in Meiji), another theory derives this “Miyake” from the Ise provincial capital granary{{Sfn|Miyake Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.
